lines.say: A ball is dropped through a light gate. Can you work out g from this graph?
This is a real A-level question from OCR Physics, June 2024, and it has two really tempting wrong answers. Pause and have a go!
Okay, let's go through it together!
The ball blocks the gate {a}from nought point one oh seconds to nought point one four. {b}That's four hundredths of a second.
In that time, the ball moves {a}its own diameter, five centimetres. {b}So its average speed is five centimetres over nought point oh four seconds, which is one point two five metres per second.
Now here's the clever bit. {a}When the acceleration is constant, the average speed is the speed at the middle of the time interval. {b}So that's the speed at nought point one two seconds.
It started from rest at t equals zero, so g is just v over t. {a}One point two five over nought point one two. {b}That's ten point four! The answer is C.
If you got {a}eight point nine three, you divided by nought point one four. {b}And twelve point five means you used nought point one oh.
Both use the edge of the interval instead of the middle. Don't worry, loads of people do that! {a}And nine point eight one is just the textbook value, not what these measurements give.
